newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower, BPA offers return.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower, BPA offers return.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Monday, reversing their recent uptrend on easing cash prices and return of Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) in the western spot market.
"It put a stop on the rally we had," said one Houston futures trader, noting the effect of BPA's return after its absence from the daily market for more than a week.
The federal agency offered next-day, non-firm power during peak hours at $11.00-12.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) and off-peak hours at $9.00-9.50.

The BPA offers indicate rising hydropower output in the Northwest after a slowdown the past several weeks due to colder-than-normal temperatures and spring spillage at the hydroelectric projects on the Snake River, traders said.
Increased hydroelectric projection as well as mild weather in the Northwest pushed the region's day-ahead power prices lower, market sources said.

Firm, peak deliveries at the California-Oregon Border (COB) for Tuesday fell to $18.50-19.00 from Friday's $19.00-20.50, while those at Palo Verde (PV) held steady at $20.00-22.00 due to fairly hot readings in southern California and the rest of the Southwest.
The power complex was also undermined by weakness in natural gas futures, brokers and traders said.
May Henry Hub gas futures, which expire Thursday, finished down 1.7 cent at $2.064 per million British thermal units.
May COB futures settled down 60 cents at $13.43 after posting a session low at $13.15. June COB ended down 58 cents at $12.87. Other COB contracts finished 20-21 cents lower.
May PV futures settled down two cents at $17.48, erasing a 25 cent gain. June PV ended down 12 cents at $18.45. Deferred PV months finished 15-17 cents lower.
Brokers and traders said they are uncertain whether today's loss is start of a downward correction. Market players would likely take cue from BPA's activity and direction of natgas futures.

Separately, three large nuclear power units in the West are currently shut for refueling and maintenance: the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 in Avila Beach, California, 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit in San Clemente, Calif., and 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Richland, Washington.

About 6,000 MW of thermal generating capacity was off-line in the West for planned and unplanned maintenance, as well as hydropower displacement sales, but some of the capacity is expected to return to service later this week.
Forecasts called for temperatures in the Southwest to run six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Tuesday, and moderate to near normal levels for the rest of the week.
Temperatures in the Northwest were forecast to be three to six degrees above normal through Tuesday with chance of rain. Temperaturees were then expected to cool to near normal levels through Friday.
NYMEX estimated 455 COB and 466 PV contracts were sold, compared with Friday's 747 COB and 292 PV lots.
